items.finding: no allocator promises an alignment: `NewGoAllocator` buffers inherit Go's 8 KiB spans, so a buffer starts at offset 0 or 8192 within a 16 KiB page and page-aligned import is a coin flip whose odds depend on heap fragmentation (measured between 5/20 and 15/20 across runs); `memory/mallocator` (libc, `NewMallocatorWithAlignment`) does give a chosen alignment, which the report as first written missed, so the remaining ask is the documentation. Related and already closed: [apache/arrow-go#70](https://github.com/apache/arrow-go/issues/70) (the C Data Interface storing unpinned Go pointers, which `runtime.Pinner` addresses)
items.title: [Memory] No allocator documents an alignment: NewGoAllocator buffers land at offset 0 or 8192 within a 16 KiB page, so page-aligned handoff to C is chance

maintainer_events.text: I believe it's not safe to share a Go-allocated buffer with C anyways (at least persistently, without pinning). https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/cgo#hdr-Passing_pointers As the referenced issue states, you should use mallocator for this, or you would need an allocator that also pins buffer…

> If a short paragraph in the memory package doc, pointing at mallocator and NewMallocatorWithAlignment for buffers that C will keep, would be welcome, I am glad to open a pull request; otherwise please feel free to close this. It would absolutely be welcome! Please do!

items.finding: in a generic `throws` function compiled at `-O` in its own module, the closure passed to `withUnsafeBytes` uses the error register x21 as scratch around an Objective-C message send and exits by tail-calling `memmove` without restoring it, so a function with no reachable `throw` reports a phantom error and the program crashes retaining it. ArrowMetal's array initialiser hit it and carries a plain-loop workaround
